$comment: Applied in order to every vendored .md file. Only mechanical rewrites live here. Everything semantic (how a Task spawn becomes a subagent call) lives in references/pi-primitives.md, which is the single instruction source. Keep this table short: a new entry needs a line in the sync log explaining why the map could not cover it.

rules.why: pstack's per-role model table lives in a Cursor rule file; ours is a JSON file the extension injects.
same table, referenced by bare name; upstream calls it a rule because Cursor stores it as one
Cursor's AskQuestion tool is pi's ask_user_question (rpiv)
Cursor's Task tool is the subagent tool
same, sentence start
poteto-agent searches the Cursor plugin dir for its own SKILL.md; ours is in the package
user skills live in the pi agent dir
project skills live in .pi/skills or .agents/skills
always-applied Cursor rules are AGENTS.md context files in pi
upstream warns against globbing other workspaces' transcripts
rules.pattern: Do(?:n't| not) glob across `~/\.cursor/projects/\*/`[,.]? ?(?:that|That) crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects[.)]?
rules.replace: Do not read other projects' session files; that reads unrelated private chats.

rules.why: pi names no transcripts dir in the system prompt; the session file is $PI_SESSION_FILE
rules.pattern: (?:under|in) the (?:active workspace's )?`agent-transcripts/` directory(?: the system prompt names| \(the system prompt names (?:this|the) path\.?\)?)?
rules.replace: in the session file `$PI_SESSION_FILE` (past sessions for this cwd: `vcc_recall` or the `sessions` MCP)

rules.why: the reflect shell snippet lists Cursor transcript layouts; pi has one session file
follows the ls snippet; pi has no legacy layouts
rules.pattern: That covers the legacy flat \(`<id>\.jsonl`\), current nested \(`<id>/<id>\.jsonl`\), and subagent \(`<parent>/subagents/<child>\.jsonl`\) layouts\. For each candidate, read the first JSONL line\. Take the file whose `message\.content\[0\]\.text` contains the conversation's opening user prompt\. If none matches, pass a tight digest of the session instead\.
rules.replace: Subagent sessions are separate JSONL files under the same sessions directory; `subagent_message` and the Subagents widget name them. If the file is unavailable, pass a tight digest of the session instead.

rules.why: orchestrate: reading local transcripts
Cursor stores worktrees under .cursor/worktrees; the user's wt tool stores them under <repo>/.worktrees
the system prompt does not name a transcripts dir in pi; the session file is $PI_SESSION_FILE and past sessions are searchable
rules.pattern: The system prompt names the workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory\. Use only that path\.
rules.replace: In pi the current session is the JSONL file at `$PI_SESSION_FILE`; past sessions for this cwd are searchable with `vcc_recall` and the `sessions` MCP. Use only this project's sessions.

rules.why: upstream warns against reading other workspaces' transcripts; pi sessions are grouped by cwd slug under ~/.pi/agent/sessions
rules.replace: Don't read sessions from other projects' cwd slugs.

rules.why: Cursor transcripts live under ~/.cursor/projects; pi sessions are JSONL under ~/.pi/agent/sessions, searchable with vcc_recall and the sessions MCP
Cursor's built-in create-skill is the authoring-a-skill playbook plus pi's skills.md
pi invokes skills as /skill:name, not /name. Only rewrite the documented pstack skill commands.
upstream recall is vendored as pstack-recall (name collision with the user's sessions-recall skill)
same rename, for prose that names the skill
upstream bro is not vendored; the user's own /skill:bro does the same job
bro is not vendored (the user owns a bro skill); the relative link would dangle

deny.$comment: Patterns that must not survive in vendored text. A hit fails the sync; fix with a rule above or a line in references/pi-primitives.md, then rerun.

exclude.$comment: Upstream skills not vendored. make-bot-ui is a Grok Bot webhook UI builder (Cursor-only). bro and recall collide with skills the user already owns; pstack's versions are kept under other names. setup-pstack is replaced by the /setup-pstack command.
